description: Ham Radio Village at DEF CON 27 covers radio frequency security and amateur radio techniques with 2 talks on RF security and antenna design.

talks.title: The RF Dark Arts
talks.summary:
In this talk at the DEF CON 27 Ham Radio Village, Jason (W2LDU) demystifies the world of amateur radio and software-defined radio (SDR) for hackers, exploring how entry-level radio frequencies provide an expansive playground for exploration. He opens by discussing the process of earning an FCC amateur radio license at 03:00, highlighting that much of the technician exam focuses on fundamental electronics, circuits, and radio wave propagation. He also showcases how digital modes like APRS (Automatic Packet Reporting System) operate at 06:00, allowing radio operators to beacon telemetry, GPS coordinates, and messages over VHF frequencies.

Jason then compares radio hardware options at 09:00, contrasting budget handheld transceivers like Baofengs with flexible RTL-SDR dongles. At 12:00, he demonstrates how an affordable USB software-defined radio receiver can monitor unencrypted transmissions across hundreds of megahertz, including ADS-B signals broadcast by commercial aircraft transponders and live weather telemetry from NOAA polar-orbiting satellites. At 15:00, he explains how regional repeater networks and linked repeater systems enable wide-area point-to-point communication across hundreds of miles.

Concluding with practical operational advice, Jason runs a live spectrum waterfall demonstration at 21:00 to illustrate how to visually identify signals across active frequency bands. At 24:00, he shares open-source decoding tools and community resources, encouraging hackers to join local ham radio clubs and experiment with SDR listening to master the radio frequency spectrum. talks.title: Hunting tape measure yagis and offset attenuators
talks.teaser: Hunting tape measure yagis and offset attenuators
talks.summary:
### Practical Direction-Finding Gear for Radio Fox Hunting
At 00:00, Mark "Smitty" (KR6ZY) presents a practical workshop on building direction-finding antennas and signal attenuators for amateur radio fox hunting at the Ham Radio Village.

### Overcoming Receiver Overload with Offset Attenuators
At 03:08, Smitty explains the operational challenges of radio direction finding. As hunters close in on a transmitter, high RF power overloads receiver front-ends, causing signals to bleed past passive resistive attenuators and making it impossible to determine directionality.

### Constructing Tape Measure Yagi Antennas
At 06:04, the speaker demonstrates how to build flexible, inexpensive 3-element Yagi beam antennas. Using steel measuring tape, PVC pipe, and a hairpin match, builders create directional VHF antennas that flex when moving through dense vegetation without breaking or losing calibration.

### Heterodyne Frequency Mixing in Active Attenuators
At 09:23, Smitty explains the electronics behind active offset attenuators. By mixing the target incoming signal (such as 146 MHz) with an internal local oscillator, the circuit produces an offset frequency that can be attenuated linearly, enabling precise signal discrimination even inches away from a transmitter.

### Field Hunting Techniques and Search Strategies
Concluding between 12:26 and 15:59, Smitty reviews field navigation techniques. He demonstrates body-shielding maneuvers and directional nulling methods to pinpoint hidden transmitters, inviting attendees to participate in hands-on fox hunting drills across the conference venue.
